issue.title: [Maintenance] Export contract follow-up
issue.body:
Reviewed SHA: dc4b2708ec2e55bb5652c2c56c8bbf640646043c
PR: https://github.com/tkubica12/pharmacy-agentic-loop-demo/pull/2 (merged, merge_commit matches reviewed_sha)

Inspected files at that revision:
- https://github.com/tkubica12/pharmacy-agentic-loop-demo/blob/dc4b2708ec2e55bb5652c2c56c8bbf640646043c/src/server.mjs
- https://github.com/tkubica12/pharmacy-agentic-loop-demo/blob/dc4b2708ec2e55bb5652c2c56c8bbf640646043c/test/server.test.mjs
- https://github.com/tkubica12/pharmacy-agentic-loop-demo/blob/dc4b2708ec2e55bb5652c2c56c8bbf640646043c/README.md

Observation: `src/server.mjs` wraps `decodeURIComponent(request.url.slice(9))` in a try/catch that returns HTTP 400 (`invalid export name`) when the export name contains malformed percent-encoding (e.g. a lone `%`). `test/server.test.mjs` covers the unknown-name (404) and encoded-traversal (404) branches, but no test exercises the malformed-encoding 400 branch, so that code path is currently unverified by the regression suite.

Suggested follow-up: add one `node:test` case requesting `GET /exports/%` (or another string that throws on `decodeURIComponent`) and assert the response is `400` with body `{ "error": "invalid export name" }`.

Acceptance criterion: `npm test` includes a passing test asserting a 400 status and that exact error body for a malformed-percent-encoding export request, with no change to production behavior.
